verdict_reason: Stripe provides a comprehensive REST API with public self-serve test keys and documentation, making it fully ready for integration.

evidence.quote: The Stripe API authenticates requests using HTTP Basic Auth. Provide your API key as the basic auth username value. You don’t need to provide a password.

The Stripe API is organized around REST. Our API has predictable resource-oriented URLs, accepts form-encoded request bodies, returns JSON-encoded responses, and uses standard HTTP response codes, authentication, and verbs.
Test mode secret keys start with sk_test_ and have unrestricted access to their sandboxes.
The Stripe API uses API keys to authenticate requests. You can view and manage your API keys in the Stripe Dashboard.
A sample test API key is included in all the examples here, so you can test any example right away.

audit_trace.skeptic_notes: The evidence provided fully supports the claims made. The API exists, uses REST and HTTP Basic Auth with API keys as usernames, provides self-serve free test mode credentials, and requires no approval to start testing.
